meta.subtitle: Mix shift and rate increases are lifting revenue per mile; maintenance, insurance and a thin balance-sheet cushion still decide whether margins follow

analystSentiment.commentary:
Covenant's second quarter of 2026 showed the revenue half of its plan working and the cost half failing. Total revenue rose {+ 9.9% +} to $332.9 million while operating income fell to $8.8 million from $11.6 million, and diluted EPS slipped to $0.32 from $0.36.

We rate the shares BUY with a $38–$48 target range. The case rests on the contract book: management is moving the asset-based fleet onto committed, longer-term contracts during what it calls the current freight market upcycle, and many of the contracts renewing over the next 12 months are, per the 10-Q, among the least profitable.

The counter-case is real. A stretched balance sheet and weak cash generation leave little margin for error, and the quarter's cost overrun shows how quickly operating expenses can absorb pricing gains. A BUY here is a bet that cost discipline catches up with pricing within the renewal window; we size the downside at a bear case of $25.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Covenant Logistics Group, Inc. is a Chattanooga, Tennessee–based provider of transportation and logistics services in the United States, founded in 1986. The 10-Q describes four reportable segments: Expedited (team-driven truckload with tight service standards), Dedicated (committed truckload capacity under contracts targeted at three to five years), Managed Freight (brokerage and transport management services) and Warehousing. The company also holds a 49% equity method investment in Transport Enterprise Leasing (TEL).

Customers include parcel freight forwarders, less-than-truckload carriers and third-party logistics providers, as well as manufacturers, retailers and food and beverage shippers; the 10-Q MD&A adds poultry feed and live haul transportation and time-sensitive loads for the U.S. government. FY25 revenue was $1.2B on net income of $7.2M, and the market capitalization was ~$856.8M at $33.76 on October 2, 2026.

thesis.label: BUY
thesis.body:
The thesis is a margin-recovery call on a carrier that is reshaping its book. Per the July 29, 2026 earnings release, Combined Truckload freight revenue per total mile rose {+ 15.1% +} in the second quarter of 2026, with over half of the increase coming from mix shift among business units and the balance from rate increases. Because average miles per unit fell {- 8.0% -}, the per-tractor gain was a smaller {+ 5.9% +}.

Those gains did not reach the bottom line because operating costs rose alongside them. Management's stated goal is to have substantially all of its asset-based business under long-term dedicated or other committed contracts by the end of this freight market upcycle, and consensus already assumes EPS climbs to $2.73 in FY27E.

We think the renewal calendar gives the plan a fair chance to show up in margins within a year, which supports BUY. The thesis fails if insurance and maintenance costs keep absorbing the revenue gains.

catalysts: Third-quarter 2026 results, where management guided to a modest sequential increase in EPS.
Renewal of the contracts covering approximately 40% of the Expedited fleet and 25% of the Dedicated fleet over the next 12 months.
Evidence that maintenance and insurance claims expense returns toward historical averages after the second-quarter spike.
A turn in Managed Freight margins once contractual rate increases catch up with capacity costs.
risks: Insurance and claims volatility, which the 10-Q MD&A ties to high retention levels and a recent Supreme Court decision.
Leverage and cash generation: net debt is 3.1x EBITDA on a trailing basis and FY25 free cash flow was negative.
Customer concentration in a small number of major customers, many in retail.
Voting influence of David R. Parker and Jacqueline F. Parker, who hold all Class B shares (two votes each) and 30.3% of Total as of the March 26, 2026 record date.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
The five-year income statement is a story of margin erosion. Operating margin fell from 9.9% in FY22 to 0.3% in FY25, and diluted EPS dropped from $3.57 in FY21 to $0.27 in FY25, even as revenue rose from $1.0B in FY21 to $1.2B in FY25.

The second quarter of 2026 brought revenue back to growth but not profit. The GAAP operating ratio worsened to 97.3% from 96.2% a year earlier, and the adjusted operating ratio worsened to 95.9% from 94.6%. Adjusted EPS was $0.42 against $0.45 in the 2025 quarter.

Earnings quality is a concern. TEL contributed $5.3 million of pre-tax earnings, or $0.16 per share, and the release says those results benefited from higher equipment sale gains. Management's own third-quarter outlook flags the absence of those higher TEL equipment sales, a lower tax rate and interest income that helped the second quarter.

The counter-case is that the mix shift is deliberate: the release explains that a smaller Expedited fleet and a larger protein-related Dedicated fleet produce fewer miles per tractor but more predictable volumes. On balance, the revenue line is improving for the right reasons, but the income statement has not yet proved the cost base can follow.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
Leverage is the constraint on the equity story. Per the 10-Q MD&A, total indebtedness net of cash (debt plus finance leases) fell {+ $6.6 million +} since December 31, 2025 to $289.7 million, primarily due to fleet downsizing and selling excess equipment.

Liquidity is adequate rather than ample. Available borrowing capacity under the Credit Facility was $59.1 million at June 30, 2026, and management says it does not expect to be required to test its fixed charge covenant in the foreseeable future. The trailing current ratio is 1.14.

Stockholders' equity was $412.9 million at June 30, 2026, against tangible book value of $232.7 million, so a large share of book value is intangible and does not cushion creditors.

On balance, the balance sheet can carry the company through a slow margin recovery, but it leaves little room for a second leg down in earnings. Deleveraging through asset sales helps, though it also shrinks the fleet that has to earn the return.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Cash flow has not covered the investment program for three years. FCF margin was negative in each of FY23, FY24 and FY25, and FY25 free cash flow was a deficit of $33.9M after capital expenditure of $147.6M. The company still returned cash in FY25, with dividends of $7.2M alongside the share repurchases discussed under capital allocation.

In the second quarter of 2026 the company distributed $1.8 million to stockholders through cash dividends.

The trailing FCF yield is -4.4%, so equity holders are not yet being paid from operations. The bull reading is that a stabilizing fleet should need less replacement capital; the 10-K risk factors list improving free cash flow and deleveraging among the strategic plan's initiatives. Until operating cash flow clearly exceeds capex, the dividend and any buybacks rest on the balance sheet rather than on surplus cash.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
Trailing multiples say little because FY25 earnings were near a trough: the P/E (TTM) is 211.0x on diluted EPS of $0.27. EV/EBITDA (TTM) is 12.2x and P/S is 0.7x.

Forward multiples carry the argument. The stock trades at 19.8x NTM earnings and ~12.4x FY27E consensus EPS of $2.73. FY26E consensus EPS is $1.70.

The consensus basis is not stated, and it matters here because GAAP and adjusted results diverge: first-half 2026 diluted EPS was $0.49 on a GAAP basis and $0.68 adjusted. Either way, the FY26E figure requires a second half well above the run rate of the opening half, which leans on the cost relief and renewals management describes.

The FY27E multiple is undemanding if that estimate holds, but the FY26E estimate looks exposed. That split is why the scenarios below value the shares on FY27E and make a fuller multiple conditional on the cost relief showing up first.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Renewals reprice the least profitable Expedited and Dedicated contracts and maintenance and insurance costs return to historical averages at the same time, so FY27E consensus EPS is delivered and the shares move to the Street median target of $52.00.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: The FY26E estimate slips but FY27E consensus EPS of $2.73 holds; once the third quarter confirms the cost relief, the market pays a fuller multiple on FY27E than today's ~12.4x, and the shares reach the low end of the Street target range, $43.00.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Either a run of large insurance claims, which high retention leaves on the income statement, or a freight market that stalls before the renewals reprice is enough on its own to cut FY26E and FY27E estimates; the market then applies a lower multiple to lower earnings, and the shares fall a little more than halfway back toward the $18.00 52-week low.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
The Base case carries a 45% weight because it requires nothing beyond the gradual margin expansion management already describes, plus a third quarter that confirms the cost relief.

The Bull case gets 25% because it needs two things to go right together: renewals that reprice and costs that normalize. The Bear case gets 30%, more than the Bull, because it has two independent routes and needs only one of them; insurance volatility is outside management's control and a stalled upcycle would leave the least profitable contracts unrepriced.

The probability-weighted fair value is $39.85, an expected upside of +18.0% against a bear-case downside of -25.9%, a reward/risk of 0.70x. That clears the BUY threshold with modest room, which is why the target range is set at $38–$48 rather than at the Bull price.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body:
The vendor data present the business as a single consolidated segment, at 100.0% of FY25 revenue of $1.2B, while the 10-Q reports the four reportable segments described in the company overview. We do not quote a revenue split between them.

The economic engine is the asset-based truckload business (Expedited and Dedicated, reported together as Combined Truckload), where the company is paid a predetermined rate per mile and its main costs are fuel, drivers, purchased transportation, maintenance and insurance. Managed Freight is asset-light brokerage whose margin depends on buying spot capacity below contract rates. The consolidated result will therefore turn on whether Combined Truckload pricing outruns its cost per mile.

moatFactors.name: Committed-capacity contracts
moatFactors.body: Dedicated contracts target three to five years, and the 10-Q MD&A says the committed structure extends the renewal cycle compared with carriers operating largely in the uncommitted market. That stabilizes volume, but the 10-K risk factors note that the company generally has no contracts guaranteeing minimum volumes and that major customers run periodic bid processes, so the protection is commercial rather than structural.

moatFactors.name: Specialized service niches
moatFactors.body: Team-driven expedited freight with standards such as 1,000 miles in 22 hours, agricultural protein haulage and time-sensitive government loads are harder to serve than general freight. These niches support pricing, yet the 10-K says the Department of War business is not subject to a contract and could be terminated at any time, and nothing in the filings shows rivals are unable to enter.

moatFactors.name: TEL equity investment
moatFactors.body: The TEL stake adds earnings from equipment leasing outside the trucking fleet's own margin. Those earnings are transactional rather than a source of pricing power, so they do not amount to a competitive advantage.

businessMoat.durability:
We assign no moat. Truckload is described in the 10-K risk factors as highly cyclical, with rates exposed to excess capacity and customer bidding, and operating margin fell from 9.9% in FY22 to 0.3% in FY25, which shows the company's niches did not protect returns through the downturn.

The committed-contract strategy can reduce volatility, and the release credits it with lowering volatility in the recent downturn. It does not create pricing power that survives a soft market, so we value the shares on cyclical recovery rather than on franchise durability.

points: Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$1.3B, up 12%, and FY27E revenue of $1.4B. Second-quarter growth of {+ 9.9% +} supports the direction, though fuel surcharge revenue did part of the work: freight revenue excluding fuel surcharge rose a slower {+ 6.6% +}.

Managed Freight freight revenue grew {+ 28.4% +} year over year in the second quarter, which the release attributes primarily to integrating assets acquired in the fourth quarter of 2025. Its segment operating ratio worsened to 98.3% from 94.2%, which the release ties to capacity costs outpacing contractual rate increases and to a 2025 surge contract that was discontinued, so the revenue growth is not yet translating into segment profit.

Dedicated freight revenue rose {+ 4.3% +} despite fewer tractors, with freight revenue per tractor per week up {+ 8.6% +} on expansion of the agricultural protein business and exits from non-specialized work. We weight this growth heavily because it is contract-backed.

Expedited freight revenue fell {- 11.4% -} as average tractors dropped {- 17.0% -}; management is deliberately shrinking toward customers willing to sign multi-year agreements. Growth here will come from price and mix, not fleet size.

Management expects its fleet count to stabilize and the share of the fleet under dedicated and committed contracts to grow. Growth from here depends on how the coming renewals price, a trade-off we set out under risks.

management.leadership:
Per the April 10, 2026 proxy statement, the named executive officers for 2025 were David R. Parker (Chairman of the Board and CEO), M. Paul Bunn (President), Tripp Grant (EVP and CFO), Dustin Koehl (EVP and COO) and Joey Ballard (EVP and CPSO). The excerpt does not give tenures.

The July 29, 2026 earnings release reads as candid: Mr. Parker said costs disappointed in the quarter, and the release quantifies the excess maintenance and insurance claims at approximately 8 cents per diluted share and a one-off benefit from a lower tax rate and interest income at approximately 3 cents. Sizing both the miss and the offsetting tailwind gives investors a way to check management's cost claims against the next quarters.

The counter-point is that the same release expects those costs not to continue at the elevated level, while Mr. Bunn acknowledges that insurance and claims expense may vary from quarter to quarter given the company's risk retention. Management's credibility on costs is therefore unproven until that normalization is visible in reported results.
management.capitalAllocation:
The 10-K risk factors list the strategic plan's initiatives as exiting unprofitable business relationships, moderately reducing the truckload fleet while growing its most profitable components, improving free cash flow, deleveraging and investing opportunistically in high-value, high-service freight. The second quarter shows the fleet and deleveraging pieces under way.

The weaker element is the sequencing of shareholder returns. FY25 share repurchases of $36.6M came in a year of negative free cash flow, so they were not funded from surplus cash generation.

Capital allocation is moving in the right direction under the stated plan, but we would want debt reduction to take priority over buybacks until free cash flow turns positive, and we would read further buybacks before then as a negative signal on capital discipline.
management.governance:
Governance facts here come from the proxy statement dated April 10, 2026. The company has a dual-class structure: Class B common stock carries two votes per share and is otherwise substantially identical to Class A, and all Class B shares are held by David R. Parker and Jacqueline F. Parker. Class B converts automatically if beneficially owned by anyone other than the Parkers or certain family members.

Compensation practices are conventional and holder-friendly on paper: annual say-on-pay votes, a CEO stock ownership guideline of six times base salary, anti-hedging and anti-pledging guidelines, a clawback policy, double-trigger change-in-control terms and no tax gross-ups. The say-on-pay resolution at the 2025 annual meeting received approximately 99.7% of votes cast. The proxy text describes the Compensation Committee's independence with reference to 2024, an odd dating in a 2026 document.

The excerpt does not state board size or how many directors are independent, and it does not give the Parkers' share of total voting power. We judge the pay framework sound in design, but the missing independence data leaves the board's capacity to check a holder with this much voting weight unverified.
management.insiderOwnership:
As of the March 26, 2026 record date, the proxy shows David R. Parker and Jacqueline F. Parker beneficially owning 7,852,474 shares: 14.9% of Class A, 100% of Class B and 30.3% of Total. All directors and executive officers as a group (13 persons) held 36.7% of Total. President M. Paul Bunn held 2.6% of Total.

Outside 5% holders include Dimensional Fund Advisors LP at 6.3% of Total, BlackRock, Inc. at 5.0% of Total and a trust holder listed under its Trust Protector and Investment Manager at 8.0% of Total.

Insider ownership aligns management with equity value, which we view as a positive for a recovery story. Because each Class B share carries two votes, the Parkers' voting weight exceeds their economic share and places them well ahead of any other holder in the table, though the excerpt does not show a majority. That gives them strong blocking influence, so outside holders should expect the long-term contract strategy to proceed on management's timetable even if the margin plan stalls.

idiosyncratic: Insurance and claims: the 10-Q MD&A expects insurance and claims expense to remain volatile because of high retention levels, the potential to be uninsured or underinsured, nuclear verdicts, and possible expansion of liability to Managed Freight after a recent Supreme Court decision, which the earnings release identifies as Montgomery. A single large claim can erase a quarter's pricing gains.

Renewal execution: many of the contracts renewing over the next 12 months are, per the 10-Q outlook, among the least profitable. If customers refuse higher rates, the company faces a choice between lower volume and continued thin margins.

Customer concentration: the 10-K risk factors say a significant portion of revenue comes from a small number of major customers, with a substantial portion of freight from retail, and that these customers run bid processes, including currently as of the February 2026 filing.

Managed Freight squeeze: the release says sourcing quality carrier capacity below contractual freight pricing remains challenging as supply exits the market. Brokerage margins could stay compressed for as long as the upcycle tightens supply.
Government business: the 10-K risk factors say the business with the Department of War is not subject to a contract, requires significant compliance work and could be terminated at any time.
risks.systemic:
The 10-K risk factors describe the truckload industry as highly cyclical and list recessionary cycles, customer inventory changes, excess trucking capacity, driver shortages, interest rates, inflation, insurance costs and changes in trade policy and tariff rates among the factors largely beyond the company's control. The retail concentration ties volumes to consumer spending and unemployment.

The thesis is explicitly cyclical: management frames its strategy around the current freight market upcycle. If that upcycle fades before the renewal calendar runs its course, the company would be left with a smaller fleet, leverage of 3.1x net debt to EBITDA and margins that never recovered.

body: We rate Covenant Logistics Group BUY with a $38–$48 target range against a $33.76 share price. The range sits below the Street consensus target of $51.75 because we do not underwrite the cost normalization that consensus EPS needs until the second half of 2026 shows it.

The two signals to watch are the third-quarter 2026 results against management's guidance of a modest sequential EPS increase, and the pricing achieved on the Expedited and Dedicated renewals over the next 12 months. Consistent progress on both would move us toward the Bull case; another quarter of elevated maintenance and insurance expense, or renewals that go the wrong way on the trade-off set out under risks, would push us to HOLD.
